# Tooltip

A small hint shown on hover or focus. Positioning, hover-intent and a11y come from Tippy.js in headless mode - Koala owns the bubble's markup, styled with our tokens. The one component built on a non-Radix primitive.

```tsx
<Button iconOnly aria-label="Save changes">
  <FloppyDisk />
</Button>
```

## Installation

```bash
# One-time setup (tokens + lib helpers)
npx koalaui-cli@latest init

# Add this component (its dependencies come along)
npx koalaui-cli@latest add tooltip
```

Manual: run `npm install tippy.js`, then copy the source into `components/ui/tooltip/` and adjust the import paths to your project. Components pull `cn` from `lib/utils`, the `tv` wrapper from `lib/tv`, and (for multi-part components) `createContext` from `lib/create-context`.

## Usage

```tsx title="usage.tsx"
import { FloppyDisk } from "@phosphor-icons/react"
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"
import { Tooltip } from "@/components/ui/tooltip"

export function Example() {
  return (
    <Tooltip content="Save changes">
      <Button iconOnly aria-label="Save changes">
        <FloppyDisk />
      </Button>
    </Tooltip>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
import {
  Tooltip,
  TooltipGroup,
  TooltipHeader,
  TooltipHeaderText,
  TooltipTitle,
  TooltipDescription,
  TooltipValue,
  TooltipSeparator,
  TooltipSection,
  TooltipStat,
} from "@/components/ui/tooltip"

<TooltipGroup>
  <Tooltip content="...">
    <button />
  </Tooltip>
</TooltipGroup>

<Tooltip
  variant="graph"
  content={
    <>
      <TooltipHeader>
        <TooltipHeaderText>
          <TooltipTitle />
          <TooltipDescription />
        </TooltipHeaderText>
        <TooltipValue />
      </TooltipHeader>
      <TooltipSeparator />
      <TooltipSection>
        <TooltipStat label="..." value="..." />
      </TooltipSection>
    </>
  }
>
  <button />
</Tooltip>
```

## Variants

`variant` sets the content shape. `text` (the default) is a short label on an inverted chip, the page's ink as its ground, so it reads at a glance and never passes for a card. Switch to `graph` when the content is a multi-line card (a title plus stats, a picture, a route): it moves onto the popover surface with Popover's border and shadow, drops the centering for a left-aligned block and adds `8px 12px` padding so the rows aren't cramped against the edge.

```tsx
// Short label - the default
<Tooltip content="Save changes">…</Tooltip>

// Rich data card - left-aligned, roomier padding
<Tooltip
  variant="graph"
  content={
    <div className="space-y-0.5">
      <div className="font-medium text-popover-foreground">Trail Runner GTX</div>
      <div className="text-muted-foreground">1,284 units · 100% of #1</div>
      <div className="text-muted-foreground">$92,448 revenue · +14% MoM</div>
    </div>
  }
>
  <Button variant="outline" iconOnly aria-label="Product stats">
    <ChartBar />
  </Button>
</Tooltip>
```

## Data breakdown

For a richer `graph` tooltip, compose the breakdown parts instead of hand-rolling markup: `TooltipHeader` / `TooltipValue` for the title and total, `TooltipSeparator` for the rule, and `TooltipSection` + `TooltipStat` for tone-railed rows of label / percent / value. The rail color is a token role via `tone` (`brand · info · success · warning · destructive · neutral`), so it tracks the theme - no raw colors. Mark sub-lines with `indent`.

```tsx
<Tooltip
  variant="graph"
  placement="right"
  content={
    <>
      <TooltipHeader>
        <TooltipHeaderText>
          <TooltipTitle>Friday, Jul 5</TooltipTitle>
          <TooltipDescription>Total capacity</TooltipDescription>
        </TooltipHeaderText>
        <TooltipValue>08h 00m</TooltipValue>
      </TooltipHeader>
      <TooltipSeparator />
      <TooltipSection tone="info">
        <TooltipStat label="Tracked time" percent="40%" value="03h 09m" />
        <TooltipStat label="Billable" percent="79%" value="02h 30m" indent />
        <TooltipStat label="Non-billable" percent="21%" value="00h 39m" indent />
      </TooltipSection>
      <TooltipSection tone="neutral">
        <TooltipStat label="Remaining capacity" percent="60%" value="04h 50m" />
      </TooltipSection>
    </>
  }
>
  <Button variant="outline" iconOnly aria-label="Day capacity">
    <Clock />
  </Button>
</Tooltip>
```

## Rich card

The graph variant grows as far as a preview card: a picture, a mark, a title with its status, and a few facts, built from the same parts as the data card. It stays a tooltip as long as it only shows: it opens on hover and focus and holds nothing to click. The moment it needs a button, a form or more than one link, it is a Popover. Keep the picture's corner concentric with the card (8px inside a 16px card) and give it the hairline image outline.

```tsx
<Tooltip
  variant="graph"
  className="w-72"
  content={
    <>
      <img src="/pages/templates/urban-luxe-neo.jpg" alt="" className="aspect-video rounded-sm object-cover" />
      <TooltipHeader>
        <TooltipHeaderText>
          <TooltipTitle>Urban Luxe Neo</TooltipTitle>
          <TooltipDescription>Interior studio template</TooltipDescription>
        </TooltipHeaderText>
        <TooltipValue>New</TooltipValue>
      </TooltipHeader>
      <TooltipSeparator />
      <TooltipSection tone="brand">
        <TooltipStat label="Pages" value="12" />
        <TooltipStat label="Sections" value="48" />
      </TooltipSection>
    </>
  }
>
  <a href="/templates/urban-luxe-neo">Urban Luxe Neo</a>
</Tooltip>
```

## Placement

`placement` takes any Tippy placement (each also accepts a `-start` / `-end` suffix). The bubble grows out of the edge nearest the trigger.

The bubble is positioned `fixed`, so one that lands past the edge of the screen is clipped there instead of widening the page: a phone never scrolls sideways because of a tooltip. While it is up it follows its trigger when the trigger moves (a drawer sliding in, a row that grows), rather than staying where the trigger was when it opened.

```tsx
<Tooltip content="Tooltip" placement="top">…</Tooltip>
<Tooltip content="Tooltip" placement="right">…</Tooltip>
<Tooltip content="Tooltip" placement="bottom">…</Tooltip>
<Tooltip content="Tooltip" placement="left">…</Tooltip>
```

## With an icon

`content` is any node - a leading glyph sits a 4px gap from the label. Pair it with an icon-only button that would otherwise have no visible name.

```tsx
<Tooltip
  content={<><Copy /> Copy to clipboard</>}
>
  <Button variant="ghost" iconOnly aria-label="Copy">
    <Copy />
  </Button>
</Tooltip>
```

## Interactive

`interactive` keeps the tooltip open while the pointer is over it, so it can hold a link or action. Tune the hover-intent with `delay` (`[open, close]` in ms).

```tsx
<Tooltip
  interactive
  delay={[150, 80]}
  content={<>Read the <a href="/docs" className="underline">docs</a></>}
>
  <Button variant="outline" iconOnly aria-label="More info">
    <Info />
  </Button>
</Tooltip>
```

## Controlled

Pass `open` to drive the bubble yourself: the hover and focus triggers switch off, and it shows exactly while `open` is true. Use it for a hint that answers an action rather than a hover, like a copy confirmation.

```tsx
const [copied, setCopied] = React.useState(false)

<Tooltip open={copied} content="Copied to clipboard">
  <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => { copy(); setCopied(true) }}>
    Copy command
  </Button>
</Tooltip>
```

## Anchored to a point

Some things have no element to hang a tooltip on: a pin drawn on a map, a point on a chart, whatever sits under the cursor on a canvas. Give the tooltip an `anchor` instead of a child, the point in viewport coordinates (or a box, with `width` and `height`), and drive `open` from your own hover logic. Moving the anchor re-positions the open bubble without re-mounting it, and the bubble takes no pointer events, so it never steals the pointer it follows.

```tsx
const [hover, setHover] = React.useState<{ pin: Pin; x: number; y: number } | null>(null)

<div onPointerMove={(e) => setHover(nearestPin(e))} onPointerLeave={() => setHover(null)}>
  {/* the map, the chart, the canvas */}
  <Tooltip
    open={hover != null}
    anchor={{ x: hover?.x ?? 0, y: hover?.y ?? 0 }}
    variant="graph"
    content={<PinCard pin={hover?.pin} />}
  />
</div>
```

## Group

Wrap a set of tooltips in `TooltipGroup` to share a single bubble that *glides* from trigger to trigger - a Tippy singleton under the hood. Instead of each tooltip fading out and then in with its own delay, the bubble repositions instantly with a CSS `transform` transition. Use this for toolbars, avatar stacks, or any dense row of labeled controls.

```tsx
import { Tooltip, TooltipGroup } from "@/components/ui/tooltip"

<TooltipGroup>
  <Tooltip content="Edit" placement="top">
    <Button variant="ghost" iconOnly aria-label="Edit">
      <PencilSimple />
    </Button>
  </Tooltip>
  <Tooltip content="Copy" placement="top">
    <Button variant="ghost" iconOnly aria-label="Copy">
      <Copy />
    </Button>
  </Tooltip>
  <Tooltip content="Save" placement="top">
    <Button variant="ghost" iconOnly aria-label="Save">
      <FloppyDisk />
    </Button>
  </Tooltip>
  <Tooltip content="Delete" placement="top">
    <Button variant="ghost" iconOnly aria-label="Delete">
      <Trash />
    </Button>
  </Tooltip>
</TooltipGroup>
```

The `delay` and `offset` props on individual `Tooltip`s inside a group are ignored - set them once on `TooltipGroup`.

## Around an icon-only Button

An `iconOnly` Button already shows its `aria-label` as a tooltip. Wrap it in your own `Tooltip` (for a keycap, a longer hint, another placement) and the Button's hint stands down, so there is one bubble, never one above and one below. The same holds through an `asChild` trigger such as `PopoverTrigger`, for any button inside the wrapped element, and for the hints other components add on their own (ToggleGroupItem, ToolbarButton, DockItem, SidebarItem, SelectItem). No `tooltip={false}` needed.

```tsx
<Tooltip content={<>Search <Kbd size="sm">⌘K</Kbd></>}>
  <Button variant="outline" iconOnly aria-label="Search">
    <MagnifyingGlass />
  </Button>
</Tooltip>

<Popover>
  <Tooltip content="Display settings">
    <PopoverTrigger asChild>
      <Button variant="outline" iconOnly aria-label="Settings">
        <GearSix />
      </Button>
    </PopoverTrigger>
  </Tooltip>
  <PopoverContent>…</PopoverContent>
</Popover>
```

Building a component that adds a hint of its own? Pass `auto` to that Tooltip and it yields the same way. A popover's content portaled from inside the wrapped element keeps its own hints.

## On form inputs

Wrap an `InputSuffixButton` in a `Tooltip` to surface field hints - password rules, format requirements, contextual help - without cluttering the label. Place the button directly inside `InputRoot` (not inside `InputSuffix`, which is `aria-hidden`) so keyboard users can reach it.

```tsx
<div className="w-72 space-y-4">
  <div className="space-y-1.5">
    <label className="text-sm font-medium">API key</label>
    <InputRoot>
      <InputField placeholder="sk-…" />
      <Tooltip content="Your secret key - never share this publicly">
        <InputSuffixButton aria-label="API key help">
          <Question />
        </InputSuffixButton>
      </Tooltip>
    </InputRoot>
  </div>
  <div className="space-y-1.5">
    <label className="text-sm font-medium">Webhook URL</label>
    <InputRoot>
      <InputField placeholder="https://…" />
      <Tooltip
        content="Must be HTTPS and return 200 within 5 s"
        placement="right"
      >
        <InputSuffixButton aria-label="Webhook URL requirements">
          <Info />
        </InputSuffixButton>
      </Tooltip>
    </InputRoot>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Inside a dialog

Tippy appends its bubble to `document.body`, so tooltips always render above the dialog's stacking context - no extra `z-index` or portal config required. A small icon next to a form label is the most common pattern.

Focus opens a tooltip only when it is keyboard focus. A dialog or drawer opened with a click or a tap moves focus onto its first control by script, and that shows no bubble; opened from the keyboard, the focused control shows its hint like any other. To drop focus hints altogether, as the help icons below do, pass `trigger="mouseenter"`.

```tsx
<Dialog>
  <DialogTrigger asChild>
    <Button>Open dialog</Button>
  </DialogTrigger>
  <DialogContent size="sm">
    <DialogHeader>
      <DialogTitle>Create webhook</DialogTitle>
      <DialogDescription>
        Koala will POST a JSON payload to this URL on each event.
      </DialogDescription>
    </DialogHeader>
    <div className="space-y-4">
      <div className="space-y-1.5">
        <div className="flex items-center gap-1.5">
          <label className="text-sm font-medium">Endpoint URL</label>
          <Tooltip content="Must be HTTPS and publicly reachable" trigger="mouseenter">
            <button
              type="button"
              aria-label="Endpoint URL help"
              className="rounded text-muted-foreground transition-colors duration-fast ease-out hover:text-foreground focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-1 focus-visible:ring-brand"
            >
              <Info className="size-3.5" />
            </button>
          </Tooltip>
        </div>
        <InputRoot>
          <InputField placeholder="https://…" />
        </InputRoot>
      </div>
      <div className="space-y-1.5">
        <div className="flex items-center gap-1.5">
          <label className="text-sm font-medium">Secret</label>
          <Tooltip
            content="Signs the X-Koala-Signature header"
            placement="right"
            trigger="mouseenter"
          >
            <button
              type="button"
              aria-label="Secret help"
              className="rounded text-muted-foreground transition-colors duration-fast ease-out hover:text-foreground focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-1 focus-visible:ring-brand"
            >
              <Lock className="size-3.5" />
            </button>
          </Tooltip>
        </div>
        <InputRoot>
          <InputField placeholder="whsec_…" />
        </InputRoot>
      </div>
    </div>
    <DialogFooter>
      <DialogClose asChild>
        <Button variant="ghost">Cancel</Button>
      </DialogClose>
      <Button>Create webhook</Button>
    </DialogFooter>
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>
```

## Keyboard shortcut hint

Include a `Kbd` in `content` to pair an action name with its shortcut. On the inverted chip the key is built from the chip's own ink, so the same `Kbd` reads on both variants. Combine with `TooltipGroup` on a toolbar so the bubble glides between buttons instead of re-fading.

```tsx
<TooltipGroup>
  <Tooltip
    placement="bottom"
    content={
      <>New file <Kbd size="sm" className="ml-1">⌘N</Kbd></>
    }
  >
    <Button variant="ghost" iconOnly aria-label="New file">
      <FilePlus />
    </Button>
  </Tooltip>
  <Tooltip
    placement="bottom"
    content={
      <>Search <Kbd size="sm" className="ml-1">⌘K</Kbd></>
    }
  >
    <Button variant="ghost" iconOnly aria-label="Search">
      <MagnifyingGlass />
    </Button>
  </Tooltip>
  <Tooltip
    placement="bottom"
    content={
      <>Settings <Kbd size="sm" className="ml-1">⌘,</Kbd></>
    }
  >
    <Button variant="ghost" iconOnly aria-label="Settings">
      <GearSix />
    </Button>
  </Tooltip>
</TooltipGroup>
```

## Transitions

Both transition styles are interruptible CSS transitions - never keyframe animations - so re-hovering mid-exit retargets smoothly without resetting from the beginning.

### Shift-away (standalone)

The standalone `Tooltip` uses a shift-away effect: on exit the bubble scales to 95 % and slides a few pixels away from the trigger. The direction is derived from `data-placement` (stamped at mount from Popper.js), so the bubble always retreats toward its origin edge regardless of the configured placement.

```tsx
<Tooltip content="Shift-away on exit" placement="top">
  <Button variant="outline" iconOnly aria-label="Info">
    <Info />
  </Button>
</Tooltip>
```

```tsx title="tooltip.tsx - default transition classes"
// Opacity + scale (95→100) + directional slide driven by data-placement
"data-[state=hidden]:opacity-0 data-[state=visible]:opacity-100"
"data-[state=hidden]:scale-95 data-[state=visible]:scale-100"

// Retreats toward the nearest trigger edge on exit:
"data-[placement^=top]:data-[state=hidden]:-translate-y-1"
"data-[placement^=bottom]:data-[state=hidden]:translate-y-1"
"data-[placement^=left]:data-[state=hidden]:-translate-x-1"
"data-[placement^=right]:data-[state=hidden]:translate-x-1"
```

### Glide (singleton / group)

Inside a `TooltipGroup` the shared bubble uses the `singleton` transition variant: opacity-only on the bubble element (no scale, so it doesn’t shrink between consecutive triggers). Spatial motion is handled entirely by Tippy’s `moveTransition` - a single `transform` transition that drives the positional glide.

```tsx
// Hover slowly between the buttons to see the glide
<TooltipGroup>
  <Tooltip content="Edit"><Button …><PencilSimple /></Button></Tooltip>
  <Tooltip content="Copy"><Button …><Copy /></Button></Tooltip>
  <Tooltip content="Save"><Button …><FloppyDisk /></Button></Tooltip>
</TooltipGroup>
```

```tsx title="tooltip.tsx - singleton transition + moveTransition"
// Bubble: opacity-only (no scale jitter as it glides between triggers)
"data-[state=hidden]:opacity-0 data-[state=visible]:opacity-100"
"scale-100"  // fixed - spatial motion is not on the bubble element

// Positional glide - set on the Tippy singleton source:
moveTransition="transform var(--duration-base) var(--ease-out)"
```

### Base transition (shared)

Both variants extend the same base transition declaration. Only specific properties are named - never `transition: all` - so unrelated properties (like `background-color`) aren’t accidentally caught and the browser can composite the animation on the GPU.

```tsx title="tooltip.tsx - base transition"
// Tailwind class: "transition duration-fast ease-out"
// Expands to:
//   transition-property: opacity, transform, scale, filter;
//   transition-duration: var(--duration-fast); /* 160 ms */
//   transition-timing-function: var(--ease-out); /* cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1) */
```

## Speed & delay

The bubble always animates at `duration-fast` (160 ms) - fast enough not to block the user, slow enough to feel intentional rather than a jump cut. The three motion tokens side by side:

The easing curve - for both the bubble animation and the singleton glide - is `ease-out`: an aggressive initial velocity that decelerates sharply. It reads as snappy without being harsh, and is the right curve for any short UI enter/exit:

Hover-intent is separate from animation speed and is controlled by the `delay` prop - an `[open, close]` tuple in ms. Animation speed stays at 160 ms regardless.

```tsx title="delay examples"
// Default - 150 ms open intent, instant close
<Tooltip delay={[150, 0]} content="…">…</Tooltip>

// Interactive - give the user time to reach the bubble before it closes
<Tooltip interactive delay={[150, 80]} content={<a href="…">Link</a>}>…</Tooltip>

// Instant open (kiosk / touch UI with no hover ambiguity)
<Tooltip delay={0} content="…">…</Tooltip>

// Group - delay is set once and shared by all children. The 200 ms close delay is the grace
// period that lets the pointer reach the next trigger while the bubble is still up.
<TooltipGroup delay={[150, 200]}>
  <Tooltip content="Save">…</Tooltip>
  <Tooltip content="Copy">…</Tooltip>
</TooltipGroup>
```

## API reference

### Tooltip

A hint on hover and keyboard focus, built on Tippy.js in headless mode (the documented exception to Radix first). It renders no wrapper: the bubble is a `role="tooltip"` element mounted on the body (or the full-screen element). Every part accepts `className`, merged last; here it lands on the bubble.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| content* | ReactNode | - | The bubble's contents: a label, a label plus a glyph, or the graph parts below. |
| children | ReactElement | - | The trigger: a single element that forwards its `ref` to a DOM node. Optional only with `anchor`. |
| variant | "text" \| "graph" | "text" | `text` is the inverted one-line chip; `graph` is the left-aligned popover card for multi-line data. Ignored inside a `TooltipGroup`. |
| placement | Placement | "top" | Tippy placement: `top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left`, each with `-start` or `-end`, or `auto`. |
| delay | number \| [number, number] | [150, 0] | Hover intent in ms, `[open, close]` or one number for both. Ignored inside a group. |
| offset | [number, number] | [0, 6] | `[skidding, distance]` from the trigger in px. Ignored inside a group. |
| interactive | boolean | false | Keeps the bubble open while the pointer is over it, for a single link. Ignored inside a group. |
| trigger | string | "mouseenter focus" | Space-separated events that open it. Focus opens it only when it is keyboard focus; pass `"mouseenter"` to drop focus hints. |
| hideOnClick | boolean | true | Whether clicking the trigger hides it. Pass `false` for a toggle whose label changes on click. |
| open | boolean | - | Controlled visibility. Setting it switches the trigger events off; with `anchor` it defaults to `true`. |
| anchor | { x: number; y: number; width?: number; height?: number } | - | Hangs the bubble on a point or box in viewport coordinates instead of `children` (a map pin, a chart point). Moving it re-positions the open bubble. |
| disabled | boolean | false | Keeps the tooltip from showing. Ignored inside a group. |

| Data attribute | Description |
| --- | --- |
| data-state | `visible` or `hidden` on the bubble; drives the enter and exit transition. |
| data-placement | The resolved placement on the bubble; sets the transform origin. |
| data-variant | `text` or `graph` on the bubble, so nested parts (a `Kbd`) can adapt. |

| CSS variable | Description |
| --- | --- |
| --surface | Set on the bubble to its own ground (`--foreground` for `text`, `--popover` for `graph`) so nested controls blend with it. |

### TooltipGroup

Shares one bubble across the `Tooltip`s inside it, so it glides from trigger to trigger (a Tippy singleton). Each child keeps its own `content`, `placement` and `trigger`; the rest is set here. Renders no element.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| variant | "text" \| "graph" | "text" | Shape of the shared bubble. |
| delay | number \| [number, number] | [150, 200] | Hover intent shared by the group. The 200ms close is the grace period that lets the pointer reach the next trigger. |
| offset | [number, number] | [0, 6] | `[skidding, distance]` from each trigger in px. |
| disabled | boolean | false | Keeps the shared bubble from showing. |
| className | string | - | Classes merged onto the shared bubble. |

### TooltipHeader

The header row of a `graph` bubble: a `TooltipHeaderText` column plus a trailing `TooltipValue`. Forwards all native `<div>` props.

### TooltipHeaderText

The stacked title and description column inside `TooltipHeader`. Forwards all native `<div>` props.

### TooltipTitle

The bold title line. Forwards all native `<div>` props.

### TooltipDescription

The muted line under the title. Forwards all native `<div>` props.

### TooltipValue

A tonal value pill (a time, count or amount) in `tabular-nums`. Forwards all native `<span>` props.

### TooltipSeparator

A hairline `role="separator"` between the header and the sections. Forwards all native `<div>` props.

### TooltipSection

A group of `TooltipStat` rows banded by a colored left rail. Forwards all native `<div>` props.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tone | "brand" \| "info" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "destructive" \| "neutral" | "brand" | The rail color, a token role so it tracks the theme. |

### TooltipStat

One breakdown row: a label, an optional percent and a `TooltipValue` pill. Forwards all native `<div>` props except `children`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label* | ReactNode | - | The row label, truncated to one line. |
| value* | ReactNode | - | The value shown in the trailing pill. |
| percent | ReactNode | - | A muted share shown just before the value. |
| indent | boolean | false | Nests the row one step in, for a sub-line under a total. |

## FAQ

### Why is Tooltip the one component not built on Radix?

Tooltip uses Tippy.js in headless mode for positioning, hover-intent, and a11y, because its placement and singleton glide behavior go beyond what the Radix primitive offers. Koala still owns the bubble markup, styled with our tokens, so this is a documented exception to the Radix-first rule.

### When should I use variant="graph" instead of the default?

Use `graph` whenever `content` is more than a single short line - a title plus a couple of stat rows, like the data card shown over a chart bar. It left-aligns the block and adds 8px/12px padding so the rows breathe; the default `text` variant centers a single label with tight padding, which looks cramped around multi-line content. Inside a `TooltipGroup` the shared bubble has one shape, so set `variant` on the group, not the individual tooltips.

### How do I keep a tooltip open so I can click a link inside it?

Pass `interactive`, which keeps the bubble open while the pointer is over it. Pair it with a `delay` like `[150, 80]` so the close delay gives the user time to travel from the trigger to the bubble before it dismisses.

### What is TooltipGroup for?

Wrap several `Tooltip`s in `TooltipGroup` to share one bubble that glides from trigger to trigger (a Tippy singleton) instead of each fading out and in. Use it for toolbars, avatar stacks, or any dense row of labeled controls.

### Why are my per-tooltip delay and offset being ignored?

Inside a `TooltipGroup` the `delay` and `offset` on individual `Tooltip`s are ignored because one shared bubble can have only one timing and distance. Set `delay` and `offset` once on the `TooltipGroup` instead.

### Does a tooltip pop open when a dialog auto-focuses its button?

Only when the dialog was opened from the keyboard. Focus opens a tooltip only when it is keyboard focus: the focus a click or a tap gives, and the focus a dialog or drawer opened by one moves inside by script, show nothing. To drop focus hints altogether, pass `trigger="mouseenter"` (the default is `"mouseenter focus"`), knowing keyboard users then never see that hint.

### Can a tooltip make the page scroll sideways on a phone?

No. The bubble is positioned `fixed`, so when it lands past the edge of the screen (its trigger still sliding in with a drawer, or hugging the edge) it is clipped by the viewport instead of widening the page. While it is up it also follows its trigger as the trigger moves, so it settles next to it once the drawer is in place.

### Is a rich preview card a tooltip or a popover?

A tooltip, as long as it only shows: it opens on hover and focus, the pointer never has to enter it, and it holds nothing to click, however much it shows (a picture, a title, a status, a few facts). Once it needs a button, a form or several links, make it a Popover, which opens on click and takes focus. For a single link, `interactive` keeps a tooltip open while the pointer travels into it.

### How do I show a tooltip over a map pin or a point on a chart?

Give it an `anchor`, the point in viewport coordinates (or a box with `width` and `height`), instead of a child element, and drive `open` from your own hover logic. The bubble follows the anchor as it moves and takes no pointer events, so it can sit right under the cursor without flickering.

### Do I need to manage z-index to show a tooltip above a dialog?

No. Tippy appends the bubble to `document.body`, so it renders above the dialog stacking context with no extra `z-index` or portal configuration. While an element is full screen (a video player, a file preview) the bubble goes into that element instead, because the browser paints nothing outside it over the screen.

## Exports and dependencies

`npx koalaui-cli@latest add tooltip` writes `components/ui/tooltip/`. Import from `@/components/ui/tooltip`:

- Components and helpers: `Tooltip`, `TooltipGroup`, `TooltipHeader`, `TooltipHeaderText`, `TooltipTitle`, `TooltipDescription`, `TooltipValue`, `TooltipSeparator`, `TooltipSection`, `TooltipStat`, `tooltipVariants`, `tooltipGraphVariants`
- Types: `TooltipAnchor`, `TooltipProps`, `TooltipGroupProps`, `TooltipTone`, `TooltipSectionProps`, `TooltipStatProps`
- Koala lib helpers it uses: `tv`
- npm packages: `tippy.js`
